newsitem.title: UK: N.Ireland's Belleek Pottery to buy Aynsley China.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland's Belleek Pottery to buy Aynsley China.

text.p: Northern Ireland's Belleek Pottery Group said on Wednesday it is to buy English firm, Aynsley China for an undisclosed "multi-million pound figure".
Belleek, which includes Galway Irish Crystal, said in a statement that the purchase would bring the group's combined turnover to almost 30 million sterling and the workforce to 800.
Heads of agreement have been signed and the deal is expected to be completed by April 30, the statement said.

"Quite simply, the acquisition of Aynsley China brings the Belleek Pottery Group into the giftware premier league," said chairman George Moore who bought Belleek Pottery Ltd of County Fermanagh in 1990.
Leading brand Aynsley, of Stoke-on-Trent, was established in 1775 and has an annual turnover of 15 million sterling and 450 employees.

Belleek Pottery, whose fine parian china products sell in Ireland, Britain and have key export markets in the U.S., Canada, the Caribbean, Europe and Australia, started in 1857. It acquired substantially the assets of Galway Irish Crystal from the official receiver in May 1993.

"In terms of management expertise, product development, distribution, sales and marketing, the experience and capabilities that will be available to each of the companies is considerable," Moore said.
"It is our intention to maximise the synergy that exists and to grow the group business significantly. We will announce our development and investment plans for Aynsley in due course."
